title: Senior's toolkit: rollouts and workloads
summary: Labels, rollouts, rollbacks, scaling and one-off jobs: the kubectl commands for running workloads day to day.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: rollouts and workloads
steps.body: Shipping a new version, watching it go out and taking it back are the workload commands you will run most.

toolkit.what: Filter by label and show label values as columns. Labels are how Deployments, Services and you find pods.
flags: only pods with that label (`-l 'env in (prod,stage)'` works too)
add the `version` label as a column

toolkit.what: Waits until the new ReplicaSet is fully rolled out, and exits non-zero if it fails. Put it in every deploy script.
flags: give up and fail after this long
print the current state once instead of waiting
toolkit.when: after every apply or image change

toolkit.what: Rolls back to the previous ReplicaSet in seconds. The fastest fix for a bad release.
flags: go to a specific revision instead of the previous one
toolkit.when: a release breaks and the cause is not obvious

toolkit.what: Lists the revisions you can roll back to.
flags: show the pod template of one revision (image, env)

toolkit.what: Replaces every pod with a rolling update and no spec change. Used after a ConfigMap or Secret changed, or to clear a stuck state.
Changes one container's image and starts a rollout. Handy for a hotfix; in GitOps setups change the manifest instead.
flags: container name, then the new image

toolkit.what: Changes the replica count now. An HPA or your next apply may change it back.
flags: stop every pod but keep the Deployment

toolkit.what: Runs a CronJob once, right now, with exactly its template. The way to test or re-run a nightly job.
flags: copy the job template from that CronJob

steps.prompt: Match the rollout command to its job.
pairs: wait until the new version is fully out
go back to the previous version
list revisions you could go back to
replace every pod with the same spec

steps.prompt: Ten minutes after the 1.4.2 release, error rates jump from 0.1% to 8%. The diff looks harmless and nobody knows the cause yet. What do you run first?
options: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/api`, then investigate with the old version serving traffic
steps.explain: Restore service first, debug second. `undo` brings back the previous ReplicaSet in seconds. Restarting or deleting pods recreates the same broken version, and scaling just runs more of it.

steps.prompt: Run the `nightly-report` CronJob once, now, to test a fix.
steps.explain: `create job --from=cronjob/...` copies the CronJob's job template, so the test runs exactly what the schedule will run.

steps.prompt: Put a manual hotfix release in order.
steps.explain: Change the image, wait for the rollout to finish, then confirm the new pods and the new revision. The last two can go either way.

steps.prompt: Your deploy script runs `kubectl apply -f k8s/` and exits 0, but the new pods crash on start. The pipeline still showed green. What is missing?
options: `kubectl rollout status deployment/api --timeout=5m` after the apply, so a failed rollout fails the job
steps.explain: `apply` only means the API server accepted the change. `rollout status` waits for the new pods to become ready and exits non-zero when the rollout stalls past the deadline.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Every deploy ends with `rollout status`, and every bad release starts with `rollout undo`. Debug after service is back. Use `-l` and `-L` instead of scrolling through pod names.
